Tom (Sales): FYI — NimbusHealth just escalated. p95 on /chat-generation in eu-west1 jumped ~300ms -> ~1.2s during peak. They say no error responses, just very slow tails. They want an ETA for a mitigation and SLA discussion. CASE-9832. @Maria (PM) @Jeff (Eng)
Maria (PM): Thanks Tom. Adding to intake. Is it latency-only (no errors) and is it tied to long contexts or specific models? Any customer repro steps?
Tom (Sales): Support says long convo contexts (~4k-8k tokens) + high concurrency (~40rps for the tenant). No immediate repro script shared yet. Customer asked for a 24-48h ETA for a mitigation.
SRE Bot: [alert] routing-engine-eu-west1 p95 increased 4x between 2026-03-20T15:05Z-15:20Z. Relevant services: serving-runtime, kv-cache-manager. Link: https://alerting.redwood.internal/ALERT-7421
Anya (Support): CASE-9832 note: started 2026-03-20 15:12Z. No 5xxs, just long tail latency spikes during multi-turn threads. Attached small log excerpt below.
Anya (Support): ```
[2026-03-20T15:12:07Z] req=abcd1234 tenant=nimbus ctx_len=6200 p95_ms=1180 kv_cache_hit=false cache_flush=1
[2026-03-20T15:12:07Z] req=abcd1235 tenant=nimbus ctx_len=300 p95_ms=320 kv_cache_hit=true
```
Anya (Support): Customer says they can route traffic to another region if we recommend it, but they'd prefer a fix in eu-west1.
Jeff (Eng): Thanks — a few quick Qs: can we get a span trace for any of the slow requests? Are the slow samples always kv_cache_hit=false? If yes, likely KV cache warmup/eviction thrash under high concurrency.
Jeff (Eng): Quick mitigation options (low-effort): 1) route Nimbus to a dedicated pool in eu-west1 with warmed KV caches; 2) pin them to model-variant with shorter context window; 3) temporary autoscale bump for serving-runtime for that tenant. All are config-level changes except (3) which costs infra.
Leo (ProdOps): Routing them to a dedicated pool is doable but needs a reserved slot and small infra ticket (INFRA-789). We can provision within ~6-12 hours if approved. Cost estimate ~0.7 GPUs reserved for the burst window.
Maria (PM): Proposed triage outcome: short-term: implement 1) route to dedicated pool + warm caches OR 2) route to eu-central1 variant within 24-48h. Long-term: add "Adaptive KV-cache and tail-latency controls" to Optimize roadmap (Q2). Acceptance criteria for short-term mitigation: a) p95 <= 500ms for 1 hour under customer's repro load; b) customer confirmation; c) runbook entry updated.
Tom (Sales): Customer needs a written ETA for mitigation to include in their procurement thread. 24-48h would be acceptable to them. They also asked if this could trigger an SLA credit if repeated.
Jeff (Eng): Implementation estimate: dedicated-route + cache-warm 8-12 engineer-hours (config + infra sprint). Routing to eu-central1 variant: ~3-4 engineer-hours (config + smoke tests). Root cause deep dive (perf tracing, telemetry) ~3 weeks.
Maria (PM): OK — decision: prioritize short-term mitigation as P1 for this customer (SLA risk). Jeff, can you own the eu-central1 variant routing option as the fastest path? Leo please start INFRA-789 for dedicated slot as backup. I'll create the product intake and backlog ticket.
Jeff (Eng): I can do the routing change. Plan: 1) create canary route for 10% traffic -> eu-central1 quantized-variant, 2) monitor p95, 3) if stable, shift 100%. I’ll post a smoke test script.
SRE Bot: Ticket created: PROD-4120 — "NimbusHealth latency triage: quick mitigate + root-cause". Linked INFRA-789.
Anya (Support): Updated CASE-9832 with PROD-4120 and customer's requested ETA (24-48h). I told them we'll confirm by EOD.
Tom (Sales): Please cc me on customer comms. I'll draft the mitigation ETA note for their legal team once we have the canary timing.

Target OKR: reduce customer tail-latency regressions by 80% for Q2 customers under high-context loads.
